metadata.title: Vlaanderen in TIMSS 2023, wiskunde- en wetenschapsprestaties van het vierde leerjaar in internationaal perspectief en doorheen de tijd

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report summarizes TIMSS 2023 results for the Flemish target population (4th grade) and compares them to international and European reference education systems. The sampling design is described as a stratified two-stage sampling design with schools selected first (stratified by school network, province location, and school-level indicators related to educational disadvantage) and then classes/students sampled within schools, with replacement schools used when selected schools could not participate. The manuscript does not report the application of specific student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) nor any replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the analysis sections of this Flemish report. Because the report focuses on descriptive and comparative TIMSS outputs (means, standard errors, trends, and benchmark attainment) rather than ML model estimation, the weighting strategy at the analysis stage is not explicitly documented here.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report describes that TIMSS estimates achievement using plausible values (five PVs per student) based on item responses and context questionnaire information, but it does not document the missing-data handling strategy used for the PV estimation or for any subsequent analyses in this Flemish report. Given that TIMSS typically uses model-based estimation for PVs and complex survey procedures, the absence of an explicit missing-data method in the Flemish report represents a reporting gap for this secondary documentation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analyses for international comparisons and Flemish performance are based on the TIMSS 2023 head study (digital mode in Vlaanderen). The target population includes students in the 4th grade of regular primary education or students taught the relevant curriculum in special primary education. Exclusions at school level were applied by the international study leadership: very small schools (<5 students in 4th grade), French-language schools, and BuBaO types 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and/or 9 were excluded (about 1% of the total population). Within the sample, additional exclusions occurred when representativeness was compromised due to missing Dutch proficiency, lack of parental consent, or mental/physical/motor limitations preventing participation (4.7% of schools excluded at analysis stage). For the mode-effect analyses, two separate samples were used: the head study (digital) with 4336 students and the bridge study (paper) with 1136 students; this report primarily uses the head study for performance results.

data.outcome_summary: This Flemish TIMSS 2023 report provides descriptive and comparative results for Grade 4 mathematics and science, using TIMSS achievement estimates on the TIMSS scale (with plausible values). Vlaanderen’s mathematics mean is 521 points (SE=2.4), significantly above the international mean (503), but with a lower spread than internationally (SD 71 vs 84). Vlaanderen’s science mean is 488 points (SE=2.6), significantly below the international mean (494). The report finds no overall mode effect between paper and digital administration for mathematics (522 vs 521; t=0.16) or science (491 vs 488; t=0.57), but it does find that students without a computer at home score substantially lower in the digital mode (mathematics: 482 vs 526; science: 433 vs 494). The manuscript explicitly cautions against causal interpretation of background associations.
